questions.prompt: Why is it important for seeds to be dispersed away from the parent plant?
options: So seedlings don't compete with the parent for light, water and nutrients
So the parent plant grows taller
So seeds stay safe in the shade
questions.explain: Dispersal also lets plants reach new places.

questions.prompt: In the Seed Designer, which feature carried seeds furthest on a riverbank?
How do birds help disperse the seeds of banyan and jamun trees?
options: They eat the fruits and the seeds pass out in their droppings far away
They blow them with their wings

questions.prompt: A new plant is discovered with light seeds covered in long, silky hairs. Predict how it is dispersed and explain your reasoning.
questions.modelAnswer: It is most likely dispersed by wind. The long silky hairs act like a parachute, increasing air resistance so the light seed falls slowly and can be carried far by the wind, like madar (Calotropis) or cotton seeds.
rubric: Explains hairs slow the fall / catch the wind
